response.reason: This lens compares NL-declared contracts against exact source-inventory and closed-model identities to detect omitted/collapsed declarations, owner-scoped initial-entry defects, wrong-target endpoints, guard mismatches, and termination-cycle issues. Key findings: (1) The root-level initial edge is owned by the top-level machine (contract NL3-INIT-1) and does correctly target HumanDriving unconditionally (transition:line:19 with Power_On trigger is an ADDITIONAL edge, while transition:line:21... wait, actually the exact root initial edge to HumanDriving exists twice: once conditional-with-trigger (line 19, unreachable) and the NL3 obligation is about the power-on triggered entry, which is exactly line 19, but it is unreachable per verify_facts refuted check). (2) NL4-ENDPOINT/GUARD: HumanDriving->Autonomous transition exists (line 20) triggered by front_distance_10 but carries no guard field, only a trigger, mismatching NL4's explicit guard requirement front_distance>10 (which was encoded as an event/trigger, not a guard predicate, in the closed model). (3) NL4.2 endpoint Autonomous->HumanDriving exists at line 18 but with wrong guard content (R45RouteToken==5, an internal route variable) rather than the semantic disjunction of human_steering_cmd/brake_pressed/in(AutoFinal); the actual event carrying that disjunction is consumed only inside the Autonomous composite (lines 14/15) and converted to a route-token effect, then guarded at line 18 by the derived token rather than directly exposing the original semantic condition. (4) AutonomousMode composite has an owner-local initial edge (transition:line:12, scope=Autonomous) targeting AutoInitial, but it is refuted/unreachable per verify_facts (guarded/triggered pseudo-initial edge, EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE for Enter_Autonomous_Mode) -- this is a default-entry defect for the AutonomousMode composite governed by NL2/derived containment, distinct from the NL3 root entry. (5) Termination contract NL5-TERM-1: HumanDriving->[*] at line 21 exists triggered by Power_Off, satisfying literal endpoint existence, so omitted here per lens discipline for satisfied literal facts, EXCEPT the root final target itself is not reachable independent of the Autonomous cycle -- but that is not this lens's V1 property; deadlock/termination-stability is behavior_consequence's job, not structural contrast, so omitted. (6) auto final substate declaration and containment are both satisfied (AutoFinal exists under Autonomous per source and model), so omitted.

result.reason: This lens compares NL-declared contracts against exact source-inventory and closed-model identities to detect omitted/collapsed declarations, owner-scoped initial-entry defects, wrong-target endpoints, guard mismatches, and termination-cycle issues. Key findings: (1) The root-level initial edge is owned by the top-level machine (contract NL3-INIT-1) and does correctly target HumanDriving unconditionally (transition:line:19 with Power_On trigger is an ADDITIONAL edge, while transition:line:21... wait, actually the exact root initial edge to HumanDriving exists twice: once conditional-with-trigger (line 19, unreachable) and the NL3 obligation is about the power-on triggered entry, which is exactly line 19, but it is unreachable per verify_facts refuted check). (2) NL4-ENDPOINT/GUARD: HumanDriving->Autonomous transition exists (line 20) triggered by front_distance_10 but carries no guard field, only a trigger, mismatching NL4's explicit guard requirement front_distance>10 (which was encoded as an event/trigger, not a guard predicate, in the closed model). (3) NL4.2 endpoint Autonomous->HumanDriving exists at line 18 but with wrong guard content (R45RouteToken==5, an internal route variable) rather than the semantic disjunction of human_steering_cmd/brake_pressed/in(AutoFinal); the actual event carrying that disjunction is consumed only inside the Autonomous composite (lines 14/15) and converted to a route-token effect, then guarded at line 18 by the derived token rather than directly exposing the original semantic condition. response.reason: This lens audits root reachability, owner default-entry, reachable event-consumer coverage, stable termination, and cross-wrapper reachability using the closed FCSTM/inspection-equivalent/verify facts. Two independent frontier defects appear: (1) the root machine has two conflicting initial edges to HumanDriving ([*] -> HumanDriving : /Power_On at line 19, unreachable per verify_facts, and the unconditional [*] -> HumanDriving at line 2 of the fcstm text which is the one actually reachable per inspection_equivalent reachable_from_initial=true state list), and the Autonomous composite's own initial edge ([*] -> AutoInitial : /Enter_Autonomous_Mode, line 12) is refuted as unreachable by verify_facts (initial-entry:transition:line:12 status=refuted) and its event Enter_Autonomous_Mode has zero reachable consumers (EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE diagnostic, reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]). This is a genuine owner-local initial-entry defect for AutonomousMode distinct from the satisfied NL3-INIT-1 root entry (root->HumanDriving is satisfied via the unconditional line-2 edge, which is reachable). (2) The Power_On event itself also has zero reachable consumers per event_consumers row for Power_On, but since NL3-INIT-1's contract is about root->HumanDriving existing and reachable (which holds through the unconditional edge), that specific contract is satisfied; the conditional/triggered redundant edge at line19 being unreachable is a structural byproduct, not a violation of NL3 itself. I derive a new initial_entry contract for AutonomousMode's own composite entry (owner=Autonomous, target=AutoInitial) since NL2 (composite declaration + containment) does not itself state this entry obligation but AutonomousMode as an operating composite semantically requires a working local entry to its substates for the sub-machine to ever execute AutoInitial/AutoFinal behavior, and the closed model's own entry edge is unreachable/refuted per verify_facts. I keep the derived initial_entry candidate as W1 (predicate=null) since S2 cannot fully decide broader default-owner semantics when the endpoint edge exists but is conditional/refuted per routing discipline. I also examine the termination contract NL5-TERM-1: HumanDriving -> [*] on Power_Off exists (line21, reachable, triggers=[Power_Off]), consumer reachable, and the target is the model's own final pseudostate with no outgoing edges, so it is stable and satisfied -- no candidate. For NL4.2-ENDPOINT-1, the closed model realizes AutonomousMode->HumanDriving only through a two-step decomposition (AutoInitial/AutoFinal -> internal exit setting R45RouteToken=5, then Autonomous->HumanDriving guarded by R45RouteToken==5) whose semantic equivalence to the compound NL condition is not resolved by available deterministic facts (SMT solver_status=not_run), so I mark that contract unresolved rather than asserting satisfaction or violation. I fold the Power_On unreachable-consumer diagnostic into supporting evidence for NL3 rather than a separate candidate, since the root->HumanDriving normative obligation is otherwise satisfied by the coexisting unconditional edge, avoiding duplicate candidates on the same locus/property.

issues.expected: AutonomousMode, as the composite required to own and enter its substates (AutoInitial/AutoFinal), has an owner-local initial pseudostate edge that is unconditionally reachable whenever Autonomous is entered.
issues.observed: The only owner-local initial edge for Autonomous (transition:line:12, scope=Autonomous, source=[*], target=AutoInitial) is gated by trigger Enter_Autonomous_Mode; verify_facts.checks.non_proved marks initial-entry:transition:line:12 as refuted (has_trigger=true), and inspection_equivalent_facts records EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE for Enter_Autonomous_Mode with reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[]. Reference_inspection_facts also independently flags W_INITIAL_UNCONDITIONAL_MISSING for composite_path llms_emp_feedback_final_0040.Autonomous with first_child_name AutoInitial.
issues.reason: NL2 requires Autonomous to be a genuine sub-machine state owning its substates, which implies a proper default-entry path; the exact owner-scoped initial edge is conditional/unreachable per deterministic verify facts and diagnostics, distinct from the separately satisfied root-level entry into HumanDriving, so this is an independent owner-local initial_entry defect.
issues.requirement_quote: The autonomous mode has sub-states and is represented by a sub machine state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: AutoInitial and AutoFinal are both marked reachable_from_initial=true in inspection_equivalent_facts.states, so some path exists into the substates even though the literal owner-local pseudo-edge is conditionally gated; a reviewer could argue reachability is preserved end-to-end even though the exact default-entry edge is imperfect.
issues.title: AutonomousMode composite lacks a reachable owner-local default entry into its substates

issues.basis: verify_facts.checks.non_proved initial-entry:transition:line:12 (status=refuted, has_trigger=true, has_guard=false, scope=Autonomous); inspection_equivalent_facts.diagnostics INITIAL_ENTRY_CONDITIONAL (line 12) and EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE for Enter_Autonomous_Mode; inspection_equivalent_facts.event_consumers row for Enter_Autonomous_Mode reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[].
issues.expected: Autonomous must have a reachable initial pseudostate edge entering AutoInitial (its default substate) so the sub-machine's internal behavior (AutoInitial -> AutoFinal -> exit) can actually execute once control enters Autonomous.
issues.observed: The closed FCSTM's Autonomous-owned initial edge (transition:line:12, [*] -> AutoInitial triggered by Enter_Autonomous_Mode) is refuted as an unreachable initial entry by verify_facts (initial-entry:transition:line:12, status=refuted, has_trigger=true). The inspection-equivalent diagnostics separately confirm Enter_Autonomous_Mode has declared consumer transition:line:12 but reachable_consumer_transition_refs=[] (EVENT_CONSUMER_UNREACHABLE). There is no other initial edge into Autonomous's region.
issues.reason: AutonomousMode is described by NL2 as an owning sub-machine state, which carries an implicit expectation that its own substates are operationally enterable; the exact verify_facts refutation of the owner-local initial edge plus the exact zero-reachable-consumer diagnostic for its triggering event together constitute a precise, evidence-grounded operational entry gap distinct from the already-satisfied root entry to HumanDriving.
issues.requirement_quote: The autonomous mode has sub-states and is represented by a sub machine state.
issues.strongest_rebuttal: The inspection-equivalent state list marks AutoInitial/AutoFinal as reachable_from_initial=true, which could indicate the tool's reachability computation still treats the edge as structurally present and therefore closes the entry regardless of the trigger-consumption caveat; if the backend's default-entry semantics only require edge existence (not runtime trigger delivery) this candidate would not hold as a violation, only as an S2-decidable structural presence.

decisions.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts transitions row transition:line:20; S5 backend receipt verdict=false; NL-CONTRACT-NL4-GUARD-1 requirement quote 'when front_distance > 10, auto transport to autonomous state'.
decisions.reason: The exact bound carrier transition:line:20 has guard=null per inspection_equivalent_facts, and the S5 backend comparison (transition_guard_equals) returned verdict=false with counterexample expected='front_distance > 10', observed=null. Guard (S5) and trigger set (S3) are distinct typed properties; an opaque event name is not an evaluable guard expression, so the exact required property is absent from the exact carrier. The alternative reading that the event name substitutes for the guard is not supported by any exact fact establishing guard-equivalence and is directly contradicted by the exact guard=null field, so it is defeated rather than surviving as a competent alternative.
decisions.strongest_defeater: The opaque trigger name 'front_distance_10' could be read as an abstraction of the same condition, treating event-as-condition as an acceptable transcription of the NL 'when...' phrasing.
decisions.violated_obligation: NL4 requires the HumanDrivingMode->AutonomousMode transition to carry an explicit numeric guard front_distance > 10.

decisions.basis: inspection_equivalent_facts transitions rows transition:line:14, transition:line:15, transition:line:18; fcstm_model.text lines 14-15,18; NL-CONTRACT-NL4.2-GUARD-1 requirement quote.
decisions.reason: The exact bound direct carrier transition:line:18 has guard='R45RouteToken == 5' and no trigger, which textually differs from the NL-required human_steering_cmd trigger and brake_pressed/in(AutoFinal) guard. However, exact supplied facts (transition:line:14/line:15 setting R45RouteToken=5 upon the very trigger event named in NL4.2, from AutoInitial/AutoFinal) show the compiler-introduced token is set precisely when the original condition fires inside Autonomous, giving a second competent reading under which the decomposition is a semantics-preserving mechanical transcription rather than a distinct wrong-guard defect. Because no exact fact closes whether this token-routing produces exactly equivalent behavior (the predicate is unsupported and no SMT check was run for this comparison here), and the alternative is grounded in exact supplied transition/effect facts rather than mere possibility, this remains a competent undercutting reading rather than a settled violation.
decisions.strongest_defeater: The route-token pattern (R45RouteToken) is a mechanical compiler decomposition that routes the original disjunctive event through internal completion transitions (line:14/line:15) before testing it as a token equality on line:18, potentially preserving the same net observable behavior even though the exact guard expression differs from the literal NL-quoted condition.
decisions.violated_obligation: NL4.2 requires the Autonomous->HumanDriving transition to carry the human_steering_cmd trigger and brake_pressed/in(AutoFinal) disjunctive guard.

The closed FCSTM realizes this composite-to-state relation only indirectly through a two-step decomposition: AutoInitial/AutoFinal each fire the shared trigger to an internal [*] exit (transitions line:14/line:15, target unresolved i.e. Autonomous's own final pseudostate) setting R45RouteToken=5, and then a separate transition (line:18) from Autonomous to HumanDriving fires only when guard R45RouteToken==5 holds. stage_receipts.reason: The NL describes a top-level state machine with HumanDrivingMode (simple state) and AutonomousMode (sub-machine state with substates), an initial entry to human driving mode on power-on, a transition from human driving mode to autonomous mode guarded by a sensor condition, a transition back from autonomous mode to human driving mode guarded by a disjunctive condition referencing an internal auto-final substate, and a termination transition from human driving mode to a final state on power-off. Contracts split containment, initial-entry, transition endpoints, guard, and termination as independently violable atomic obligations. No continuous/repeated activity is explicitly stated, so no state_action contract is manufactured. No cardinality or region-count statement is made, so no cardinality contract is created. The AutonomousMode substates are not individually enumerated in NL beyond the auto-final reference used as a guard condition, so no separate containment for "auto final" is fabricated beyond what NL supports as a guard-locus reference; it is preserved as a guard hint value only.
